chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The merit of barley bread over wheat is like our merit over the people, and there is no Prophet except that he supplicated for the eating of barley and blessed it, and nothing enters the stomach except it expels every illness within it, and it is the sustenance of the Prophets and the food of the righteous. Allah the Exalted refused to make the sustenance of His Prophets to be anything except barley.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of barley in Shia tradition according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS), the physical superiority of barley over wheat is used as a metaphor for the spiritual and ontological rank of the Ahl al-Bayt among all of humanity, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical tradition. The text emphasizes that barley was the exclusive sustenance ('quoot') of the Prophets and the righteous, serving not only as nourishment but as a divine remedy that expels all diseases, thereby linking physical health to spiritual purity. This comparison underscores the unique status of the Imams as the inheritors of prophetic wisdom and bodily perfection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form Muhammad Bin Isa, form Yunus, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The merit of the barley bread upon the wheat is like our<sup>asws</sup> merit over the people, and there is none from a Prophet<sup>as</sup> except that he<sup>as</sup> for the eating of the barley, and Blessed upon it, and it does not enter the inside except it throws out every illness in it, and it is a livelihood of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and food of the righteous. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the High Refused to Make the livelihood of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> to be (anything) except for barley’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

The excellence of barley bread over wheat bread is like our excellence over the people. There had not been any Prophet, who did not ask to eat barley bread and blessed it. In whichever stomach it enters, it removes every illness thereof. It is the sustenance of the Prophets and the food of the virtuous ones. Allah, most High, disdained to make the food of His Prophets in anything other than barley.”’
